solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sort of belt to employ for holding woman together

indicators.note: the woman's name holds the other piece within it, wrapped round it

parts.note: Carol is a woman's name
to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: Someone works out what kind of belt to put on a woman to keep her together.
explanation.definitionFit: A baggage carousel at an airport is a moving conveyor belt, so it is one kind of belt.

clue.text: Rogue enters region, not a place for amusement?

indicators.note: the rogue goes into the shortened region, so it sits inside it
not a tells us one letter A is dropped from the region word

parts.note: an area is a region
a cad is a rogue or bounder

explanation.surface: A villain moves into a district, which is no fun place to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' drops one A from the region word, leaving ARE; the question mark flags the definition as a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a hall of slot machines and games, a place people go for fun.

clue.text: Smallest thing I missed on journey in region down under

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set on another comes above it, so first
the letter I is missed out, so it is left out of the tiny-thing word

parts.note: an iota is the smallest possible amount
a go can mean a trip or journey, as in a go on the train

explanation.surface: A traveller loses the tiniest item while touring somewhere in Australasia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I missed' takes the letter I away from the tiny-thing word. The answer is a region of New Zealand's South Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Down under is an informal name for Australia and New Zealand, and the region lies in New Zealand.

clue.text: Trading document giving news of decline in high street?

definitions.meaning: a receipt given to a customer when goods are bought

definitions.text: news of decline in high street?
definitions.meaning: read whimsically, a fall in what shops sell, with sales slipping

explanation.surface: A shop receipt is offered up as a report of retail falling off.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt for a purchase is a commercial record, the paper given at the till.

clue.text: Indian city in good fortune at the present time

parts.note: good fortune is luck
at the present time means now

explanation.surface: An Indian city is said to be enjoying good fortune at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh in northern India.

clue.text: Very bad cold minimised with spirit — gosh!

parts.note: cold cut down to its abbreviation C, as on a tap
rum is a spirit
my! is an exclamation like gosh!

explanation.surface: Someone whose cold was eased with a tot of spirits exclaims in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or awful, of poor quality.

clue.text: No room for litres of red wine? Mark suggests something could be squeezed in

definitions.text: Mark suggests something could be squeezed in

indicators.note: no room left for litres means their letter is removed

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine

explanation.surface: A cellar has no space for litres of red, and a mark shows where more might fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The proofreader's insertion sign, an inverted V, shows where text should be added.

clue.text: Hindu asap working out his sacred text

indicators.note: the letters are worked out into a fresh order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Hindu urgently works through his holy scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' rearranges all the letters of HINDU ASAP; 'his' points back to the Hindu.
explanation.definitionFit: The Upanishads are ancient philosophical scriptures of Hinduism.

clue.text: Holy man in ruin nearby

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
about can mean nearby, around the place

explanation.surface: A holy man is found among some ruins in the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A marabout is a Muslim hermit or saint in North Africa.

clue.text: It may be difficult to make out Schubert's original slow movement

definitions.text: It may be difficult to make out

indicators.note: the original letter is the first one of the composer's name

parts.note: a crawl is a slow movement

explanation.surface: A slow movement in a Schubert manuscript is hard to decipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slow movement' sounds musical, as in a symphony, but it means a crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy handwriting is hard to read, so this is something difficult to decipher.

clue.text: Pirates in my ship wanting ventilation

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation like my!

indicators.note: in tells us the ventilation word goes inside the exclamation and ship together

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
what the ship is wanting, or needing, is ventilation, which is air

explanation.surface: Buccaneers aboard a stuffy vessel are crying out for fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like lacking, but here it means the ship needs something; 'in' sends the airy word inside, between the two letters of the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsairs were pirates, especially those of the Barbary coast.

clue.text: A university type keeping promises is right

indicators.note: the academic keeps the promises within him

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
vows are promises

explanation.surface: A lecturer who keeps his word is said to be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is the noun: an advowson is the right to present a priest to a church living, an old English legal term.
explanation.definitionFit: Advowson is the legal entitlement of a patron to nominate a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Quivering sound curtailed by singer in novel

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, the final letter

parts.note: a trill is a quavering sound

explanation.surface: A singer's warble is cut short in a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilby O'Ferrall is the singer heroine of George du Maurier's novel of that title.

clue.text: Energy unit developed in UK worth a lot, I fancy

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters are worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone muses that an energy measure devised in Britain is valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the letters of UK WORTH A LOT I; 'fancy' just completes the musing.
explanation.definitionFit: This unit equals a thousand watts used for sixty minutes, the measure on electricity bills.

clue.text: Ma is known to be construed as such — but not pa

definitions.text: Ma is known to be construed as such — but not pa

indicators.note: construed means interpreted, so the letters are reassembled in a new reading

explanation.surface: A mother counts as a female relative, whereas a father does not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be construed' rearranges MA IS KNOWN; the rest of the clue confirms the sense, since a mother is a female relation but a father is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A female blood relation, as a mother is and a father cannot be.

clue.text: Artist first providing support for military show

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other, so comes after it

parts.note: a tattoo is a military display, as at Edinburgh
1ST, read as IST, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: An artist is the first to back a military display.
explanation.walkthrough: The numeral 1 in 1ST is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inks designs into skin is a kind of artist.

clue.text: Italian city's birds — number with their usual formation coming in

indicators.note: the number and the formation come into the birds' word

parts.note: geese are birds
geese typically fly in a V formation

explanation.surface: Birds over an Italian city arrive in their customary flying pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Genovese is the adjective for things from Genoa, as in pesto alla genovese.

clue.text: Nasty President with aim to be ungenerous

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted or warped, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spiteful head of state sets out to be stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean-spirited describes someone petty and grudging, lacking generosity.

clue.text: Somehow disposed of, one part of armed forces disappeared

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one branch of Britain's armed services
fled means ran off, vanished

explanation.surface: An airman has vanished, having somehow been got rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize that is raffled is given away by lottery, a way of getting rid of something.

clue.text: Reward for honoured folk is said to be fiddle

indicators.note: said signals that the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a medal is an award for people being honoured

explanation.surface: An honours award is rumoured to be a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like a swindle, but here it is the verb to tinker or interfere.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle with something is to tamper or interfere with it.

clue.text: Pet given front position? That's amazing!

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship, its foremost position
wow! expresses amazement

explanation.surface: An animal put at the head of things prompts an astonished cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow-wow is a childish name for a dog, the classic household companion animal.

clue.text: Ecstasy seen in something magical is diminished

indicators.note: the drug's letter is seen inside the magical item

parts.note: a wand is a magic stick
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A rush of euphoria found in a spell fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon wanes as it shrinks, so waned means grew smaller.

clue.text: Bit of a walk — Michael's got his Dizzy maybe following around

indicators.note: the turned piece follows the politician's name, so comes after

parts.note: Michael Foot was a British Labour leader, here with his possessive 'S

indicators.note: around signals that the animal word is turned round

parts.note: Michael Foot's dog was called Dizzy, after Disraeli, so an example of a pet

explanation.surface: A former Labour leader has his dog trotting round after him on a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led Britain's Labour Party in the early 1980s, and his dog Dizzy was named after Disraeli; 'around' turns the pet word back to front, TEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A single pace is one small part of a walk.

clue.text: Philosopher thus keeps almost closed

indicators.note: the Latin for thus keeps the other piece within it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
a door pushed to is shut or nearly so

explanation.surface: A thinker accordingly keeps himself nearly shut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Zeno's school, which taught calm endurance, is a member of an ancient school of philosophy.

clue.text: Revolutionary period with good end but not beginning

indicators.note: the word for end loses its beginning, its first letter

parts.note: terminal means final, at the end

explanation.surface: A time of upheaval comes to a happy conclusion though it never started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' refers to the French Revolutionary calendar, in which Germinal was the spring month.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Revolutionary calendar named its seventh month after seeds sprouting in spring.

clue.text: Lover is aged, ancient

parts.note: olde is the mock-antique spelling of old, so aged in an ancient form

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is described as elderly and decrepit.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the tragic lover of Tristan in the medieval legend and Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Like something written in prison?

definitions.meaning: a thing composed by hand is described as written down with ink
shut in an enclosure, confined like a prisoner

explanation.surface: A text composed behind bars is pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both written with a quill and shut in an enclosure such as a sheepfold.

clue.text: Investigator longed to be even-handed

parts.note: DET is short for detective
ached means yearned or longed

explanation.surface: A detective yearned to be fair-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A detached judge is impartial, standing apart from both sides.
